highest_reported.source: Konev and Lisitsa, arXiv:1405.3097v2, §4 and author data page; fixed 2026-11-06 source snapshot.
highest_reported.reproduction_status: Feasible unrestricted C=3 sequence recovered from a publicly linked notebook and exactly checked. This is a lower bound on the unknown finite maximum, not an optimality proof. The recovered text is not claimed byte-identical to the original compressed author download.

best_human.source: Konev and Lisitsa, Computer-Aided Proof of Erdős Discrepancy Properties, arXiv:1405.3097v2, §4 and author data page.
best_human.provenance: Traditional SAT-based computational construction. The paper reports an unrestricted sequence of length 130000, with its first 127600 entries completely multiplicative.
best_human.evidence_state: A full 130000-sign witness is recovered from a public Wolfram Community notebook discussing this problem and passes exact local checking. The discussion cites the Konev-Lisitsa work and author data page. Notebook data may be a re-encoding; byte identity with the original compressed file is not asserted.

best_public.source: Konev and Lisitsa, arXiv:1405.3097v2, §4 and author data page.
best_public.provenance: Published traditional SAT search; the paper reports the construction, not a proof that it is longest.
best_public.evidence_state: The paper and author page identify the 130000 unrestricted construction. The saved full witness was reconstructed from a public Wolfram Community notebook discussing this problem and independently verified.

best_reproduced.verification_method: Integer arithmetic scans every homogeneous progression difference d and every prefix length k, checking |sum(x[d], x[2d], ..., x[kd])| <= 3.
best_reproduced.origin_type: published SAT construction recovered from a public Wolfram Community notebook; exact constraint verification, original compressed-file byte identity not established

restricted_results_not_this_configuratio.status: proved exact maximum; restricted problem, excluded

optimality_status.status: open; at least 130000, exact finite maximum unknown
optimality_status.evidence: Konev and Lisitsa report the 130000 unrestricted construction but do not prove optimality. Their exact 127645 result is for the completely multiplicative restriction. The 2026 Princeton thesis concerns the solved C=2 case. Tao's theorem rules out infinite bounded-discrepancy sequences but gives no exact finite maximum.
optimality_status.limitations: Current-source survey establishes the distinction between the unrestricted and restricted problems; it does not derive a useful finite upper bound for the selected unrestricted C=3 instance.
